stem: Every morning, my grandfather ____ his dog around the park.
working: ‘Every morning’ tells us it is a habit, so we use the simple present. Grandfather is one person, so the verb takes an s: walks.
Watch out: ‘is walking’ means right now, not every morning.

stem: Mei Ling ____ her homework when the lights suddenly went out.
working: A long action (doing homework) was cut by a short one (the lights went out). Long action in the past = was/were + -ing.
Watch out: ‘did’ sounds past, but it would mean she finished her homework, not that she was in the middle of it.

stem: Each of the boys ____ a water bottle for the trip.
working: The boss of the sentence is ‘Each’, which means one. One boss takes a singular verb: brings.
Watch out: ‘boys’ is only a passenger. Don’t let it make you choose a plural verb.

stem: “Please pass me ____ markers on the far table,” said the teacher.
working: Markers = many. On the far table = far away. Many + far = those.
Watch out: ‘these’ is many but near.

stem: There isn’t ____ milk left in the fridge.
working: ‘isn’t’ makes the sentence negative, and negatives take ‘any’. Milk cannot be counted, so ‘many’ and ‘a few’ are out too.
Watch out: ‘some’ is for positive sentences: There is some milk.

stem: The cat jumped ____ the table and ran out of the kitchen.
working: The cat was on the table and left it. Leaving the top of something = off.
Watch out: ‘into’ means going inside something. You cannot jump inside a table.

stem: Ravi and I cleaned up the classroom by ____ after the party.
working: Ravi and I = we. The mirror word for ‘we’ is ourselves.
Watch out: ‘myself’ only covers me, but Ravi helped too.

stem: Our team practised very hard, ____ we still lost the match.
working: Practising hard should help you win, but they lost. A surprise or opposite idea needs ‘but’.
Watch out: ‘so’ is for a result that makes sense, like ‘we practised hard, so we won’.

stem: You have finished your project, ____ you?
working: Flip and mirror: the sentence is positive with helper ‘have’, so the tag is negative with the same helper: haven’t you?
Watch out: ‘don’t’ copies the wrong helper. Look for the helper verb already in the sentence.

stem: Mother told Marcus that he must ____ his room before dinner.
working: After ‘must’ (and can, will, should, has to) the verb goes back to its plain base form: tidy.
Watch out: ‘he’ makes you want an s, but the helper ‘must’ is bossy and takes the s away.

passage:

Ethan ran over to help ___(3)___. Finally, Ethan spotted the ball under a bush and threw it back to ___(4)___ cousin.
working: Marcus and Ethan (two people) are DOING the playing, so we need the doer word for many: they.

stem: The tired hikers ____ up the steep hill, dragging their feet.
working: The clue twins are ‘tired’ and ‘dragging their feet’. Trudged means walked slowly and heavily.
Watch out: dashed, skipped and raced are all fast or bouncy, which clashes with ‘tired’.

stem: The little boy was ____ to see the huge dinosaur skeleton. It was the most amazing thing he had ever seen!
working: ‘the most amazing thing he had ever seen’ tells us he was very surprised in a good way: astonished.
Watch out: The other three are all unhappy feelings. Check whether the clue is happy or unhappy first.

stem: Our new classmate hardly says a word. She is as quiet as a ____.
working: The saying is ‘as quiet as a mouse’.

stem: The firemen ____ the fire quickly with their hoses.
working: To put out a fire means to stop it burning.
Watch out: ‘put off’ means to delay something, like putting off your homework.

stem: We saw a ____ of fish swimming around the coral.
working: A group of fish is a school. (Herd = cows, flock = birds or sheep, pack = wolves.)

Rewrite the sentences as ONE sentence using the word given. Keep the meaning the same.

(because)
answer: Wei Jie was hungry because he had not eaten breakfast.

(Although)
answer: Although the rain was heavy, the children still played outside.
accept: Although the rain was heavy, the children played outside.

stem:
Arrange the words to make a correct sentence. Remember the capital letter and the full stop.

[the bus] [were waiting] [arrived] [when] [we] [at the stop]
answer: We were waiting at the stop when the bus arrived.
accept: When the bus arrived, we were waiting at the stop.
working: Find WHO first (we), then WHAT they were doing (were waiting at the stop), then join the second part with ‘when’.
marking: 2 marks for the full correct sentence; 1 mark if one chunk is out of place or the capital/full stop is missing.

stem: Why did Nathan bring Biscuit home?
passage:
**The Missing Hamster**

Nathan’s class had a pet hamster named Biscuit. Every Friday, one pupil took Biscuit home for the weekend. This Friday, it was finally Nathan’s turn. He carried the cage home carefully and placed it on his desk.

On Saturday morning, Nathan woke up and rushed to say hello. His heart sank. The cage door was open and Biscuit was gone! Nathan searched under his bed, behind the curtains and inside his cupboard, but there was no sign of the hamster.

"What will I tell my teacher?" he cried. His older sister, Joanne, heard him and came to help. She noticed a trail of tiny seeds on the floor. "Biscuit must have dragged **them** out of his food bowl," she said. The two of them followed the trail into the kitchen.

There, curled up in a sock inside the laundry basket, was Biscuit, fast asleep. Nathan let out a sigh of relief and gently put him back in the cage. This time, he checked the door twice.

On Monday, Nathan told his teacher everything that had happened. Instead of scolding him, she thanked him for being honest. From then on, Nathan always checked every latch he closed.
options: He had just bought the hamster.
It was his turn to look after the class pet.
working: Paragraph 1: ‘one pupil took Biscuit home’ every Friday, and ‘it was finally Nathan’s turn’.

"What will I tell my teacher?" he cried. His older sister, Joanne, heard him and came to help. She noticed a trail of tiny seeds on the floor. "Biscuit must have dragged **them** out of his food bowl," she said. The two of them followed the trail into the kitchen.

There, curled up in a sock inside the laundry basket, was Biscuit, fast asleep. Nathan let out a sigh of relief and gently put him back in the cage. This time, he checked the door twice.
